need: Place a gate between two posts or fence ends as a readable opening: an open leaf or panel with a visible frame, hinge posts that match the fence, and no lantern or stray block that reads as a pillar.
evidence: Rejected 'Make the garden gate read as a gate': a bare light block with a floating lantern beside the post reads as a stray unfinished pillar, and the open gate, fence and ivy were removed.

need: Chimney stacks should project a set height above the roof surface and take a dark cap material by default, with a check that the cap is not sunk into the roof covering or lit as a bright patch.
evidence: Rejected 'Chimney on the west gable': a single bright pale cap sunk into the dark slate reads as a light patch or hole, not a stack, and is barely visible at a glance.

tool: glance render (small roof and wall features)
need: The glance render should show small roof and wall features (chimney caps, signs, fixtures) at the distance the judge sees the whole building, so a feature that disappears at glance scale is flagged.
evidence: Rejected chimney: judged 'barely visible at a glance'. Rejected curtains: 'the street view looks the same as before'.

need: Before placing a sign, board or banner, check clearance from adjacent signs and fixtures on the same wall and refuse or warn when two signs would touch and merge into one banner.
evidence: Rejected 'Hang a second small sign by the barrel': the dark board butts directly against the READING ROOM sign so the two merge into one long banner, and the dark oak clashes with the lighter board.

need: Window dressing should be recessed inside the opening with a depth offset, and a clash check should block placement over hanging lanterns, signs or other wall-mounted props.
evidence: Rejected 'Curtains on the side and back windows': a flat, translucent red strip overlaps the hanging lantern and the wall beside the window, so the back window reads as cluttered.

need: Flag any block whose luminance or saturation is far outside the build's aged palette, and suggest a weathered block of the same role before placement. A pure white block on a mossy build should not pass.
evidence: Rejected 'Operator touch: clean quartz doorstep': a pure white quartz step is a stark bright patch against mossy grey stone, reading as a mismatched, unweathered tile.

need: An opening option for door and window reveal depth, so the frame sits recessed by a set number of blocks and casts a visible shadow edge, rather than being recoloured on the wall face.
evidence: Rejected 'Fix walkability readout and door reveal': the door-side panel was recoloured to dull grey and brown, which removed colour but did not visibly improve the door reveal at a glance.

need: Sign placement should take a legibility/size option, such as a minimum letter height or a fixed text-to-width ratio, and reject or warn when the sign text is smaller than a readable size at the target scale.
evidence: Rejected 'Make the sign legible and prominent': sign text unreadably tiny; the fix didn't make it more legible or prominent.

tool: fascia / sign band placement with opening clearance
need: A band or fascia brush that places a sign or beam only in solid wall zones above the openings and reports any overlap with window or door cells before it is applied.
evidence: Rejected sign task: new oak beam across the upper storey is a wide plain slab that covers the windows, so the window row looks blocked.

tool: gable apex cap / stepped peak (attached to the roof)
need: A brush that builds a stepped cap on a gable apex, with each course bonded to the roof and wall cells beneath it, so no block is left floating or detached.
evidence: Rejected 'Stepped stone peak above the gable': a boxy, detached stone lump floats above the gable with a visible hole beside it.

tool: palette by role (post / corner material for dark stone walls)
need: Corner and post material defaults should be chosen by contrast with the wall material role, and the palette check should flag wood posts or logs set against dark stone walls.
evidence: Rejected stepped-peak task: stripped log corner posts clash with the dark stone walls, so the roofline looks less crafted.

need: The renderer should offer an interior or through-window view, so that interior changes such as shelving and meeting rooms can be judged when they are not visible from outside.
evidence: Rejected 'Interior stock and meeting room': the changes are barely visible from outside, so the judge cannot see the work.

tool: lean-to / addition brush with wall-and-roof attachment
need: A lean-to or addition brush that bonds its roof to the host wall and sets its wall cells against the existing envelope, with an orphan-block check that flags any block with no solid face contact.
evidence: Rejected 'Plank/wool lean-to': a patchy strip of wool and plank bands, and a stray red cube sticks out from the side.

need: A check that lists every block with no face-adjacent support or structural connection to the build, so stray or floating cubes are caught before render review.
evidence: Stray red cube on the lean-to and detached stone above the gable; both were visible only in the render.

tool: palette by role (wool and other non-facade blocks on facades)
need: Palette-by-role guidance or a validator should reject wool and other non-architectural blocks as facade or roof material unless the role is marked as decorative.
evidence: Rejected lean-to: red and yellow wool blocks read as clutter on a building facade.

tool: glance-scale check (new, in the render/check step)
need: Report every detail whose on-screen footprint at the glance distance is below a threshold (e.g. a 1-block accent, a sign's small text, sparse patches), so builders see which details will vanish before judging.
evidence: Five rejections say the same thing: the plaque text, the lanterns, the quartz kick-plate, the weathered base and the roof texture are all too small or too sparse to read at a glance.

need: A plaque preset with a legible text scale and a gold-trim or gold-leaf frame option, so a name plate reads as gold lettering from the glance distance.
evidence: 'Make the name plaque legible and gold' was rejected: the text was unreadable and the plaque was not visibly gold.

tool: emblem / pictogram inlay on a gable or tympanum field (B.emblem, new)
need: Place a recognisable symbol (e.g. a scales or seal motif) as a contiguous, readable inlay inside a named wall field such as a pediment, using a small pattern library and a palette contrast rule.
evidence: 'Make the pediment seal read' was rejected: the bright quartz panels read as stray white patches, not as a seal.

need: A surface pattern option for roof coverings (staggered or mixed-block courses, tile-course rhythm, or a per-course tone alternation) with a contrast setting, so slopes read as crafted rather than as a flat single-material field.
evidence: 'Texture the roof slopes' was rejected: the slopes still read as flat grey stone-brick courses, and the added texture was barely perceptible.

need: Weathering presets with a minimum coverage and contrast floor for a band (e.g. a base course), so moss and cobble patches are visible at the glance distance rather than sprinkled sparsely.
evidence: 'Weathered base on the flanks and rear' was rejected: a few mossy and cobble patches were barely visible in either view.

tool: lantern / light fixture anchored to architectural features (B.lantern, new, or a placement option on pilaster caps and posts)
need: Attach lanterns to a named feature top (pilaster cap, post top, wall top) by role instead of by coordinates, at a size that reads at the glance distance, and check that the light source does not add a stray colour cast.
evidence: 'Lamps on the side pilaster caps' was rejected: the lanterns were tiny specks, did not sit on the caps, and the build had no pilaster-cap placement rule.

need: A sill or kick-plate treatment that spans the full width of the opening as a continuous band, not one or two cells, with a default that defeats the stray-block look.
evidence: 'Clean quartz kick-plate under the east gallery windows' was rejected: the strip was a tiny accent that read as a stray bright block, not as a kick-plate.

tool: mcd render (per-job before/after diff + close-up crop)
need: For each detail job, render a before/after pair with a changed-cell count and a zoomed crop of the changed region, so sub-block edits are visible to the judge. A job that changes 0 cells must report 0, not look like a successful no-op.
evidence: About 25 'no visible change' observations across jobs (e.g. 'A and B pixel-identical in all four views', 'changes too subtle to read'). Full-size views cannot show 1-block texture.

need: Default variants must change colour value or relief by a visible step (a contrasting block family or a 1-block recess), and any variant below a minimum contrast should be rejected. Same-family near-tone swaps read as no-ops.
evidence: Wall field variation (deepslate, west flank, front) invisible; roof tile variation identical; shaft flank banding and elevator-head banding invisible; chimney texture invisible; deepslate lintels same colour as surround; pier grain only subtle.

need: A band option that projects the course one block proud and runs continuously between storeys on every face, so storey lines read in the silhouette.
evidence: Mid string course between storeys not visible in either render; shaft flank storey bands add no visible profile.

need: A projecting hood (slab or stair cap) over each opening head, with a proud-depth parameter, so window heads cast a visible shadow line.
evidence: Drip hoods over every window produced pixel-identical renders, or were too small to see.

need: Capital and end-cap options for piers and sign bands, so pillar tops and band ends are distinct from the shaft.
evidence: Entrance sign band end-caps and pillar capitals show no visible change in either build.

need: Default lantern placement should mount on a visible post or bracket at door height, sized to resolve at full view. Lanterns placed at default positions are lost at render scale.
evidence: Portico base lanterns not visible in either render; the job added no discernible detail.

need: Coping must be one continuous course on the wall-top ring. Stray placement off the ring is a defect, and the job should fail if the ring is not closed.
evidence: Roof-edge coping left stray specks on the rooftop with no edge improvement; roof-line coping on the front frieze not visible.

need: Options for a base flare or plinth ring and a shoulder corbel ring on towers and drums, so the base and shoulder read in the silhouette.
evidence: Tower base and shoulder: the only change was faint block texture on the shaft; the base and shoulder did not improve.

need: A weathering variant (mossy or cracked stone, darker step) reachable from detailing, not only from landscaping moss, so the base reads as weathered.
evidence: Mossy weathered base and plinth weathering/moss invisible; the stepped plinth in one build was the only visible change.

need: Opening and lintel jobs should enumerate openings from the element map per face. A job with zero targets must report a blocker, not write nothing and pass silently.
evidence: Window lintels (front and west flank) and the back door frame showed no change; the back door is not visible in either render, so the job likely had no target.

need: Report cells written per rule and warn or fail when a rule writes zero cells, so a no-op detail job is caught before review instead of being judged as a finished change.
evidence: Detail jobs 'Eaves cornice, west wall top', 'Stair-shaft glazing grid', 'Roof edge trim, north gable and shaft head' and 'Roof edge' each changed no visible pixels in any view.

tool: roof edge trim / coping / eaves cornice
need: Give roof-edge treatments a default projection and course depth that reads at full-build scale, so a coping or trim change is visible without hand-tuning sizes.
evidence: 'Roof edge' (JOB 11) had only a tiny vent and cap change; 'Roof edge coping' (JOB 10) showed no meaningful roof-edge profile at street view.

tool: weathering / speckle treatment (mcd paint vary, mossy and cracked variants)
need: Weather by contiguous course or panel with a coverage fraction and clustering, instead of scattering single cracked or mossy blocks that read as random noise.
evidence: Plinth mossy and cracked variation, wall-field cracked-deepslate patches, shaft-wall and elevator-head stone swaps, oak chute plank patches and wall texture were all judged faint, random speckle.

need: Default to a projection depth that casts a visible profile line over the full opening width, so sills and lintels read as profiles rather than sparse stubs or nothing.
evidence: 'Upper window lintels (front)' showed no visible lintel profile; 'Upper window sills (side)' added only tiny sparse plank stubs.

need: Accept an avoid or protected-cell set (as landscaping's avoidCells does) so sill, lintel and trim passes never cut into pilasters, piers or other reserved cells.
evidence: 'Window sills and lintels (north)' added ragged dark blocks that cut into the timber pilasters and cluttered the elevation, making it worse.

need: Provide a pilaster capital and base brush built from stair and slab courses in a specified material, so capitals and bases read as crafted profiles without stray diagonal bands. Cause not yet verified; the observation alone does not show whether the bands came from orientation, material or geometry.
evidence: 'Pilaster capitals and bases (north)' added large flat grey diagonal bands across the white portico and pilasters, which read as artifacts and broke the clean portico.

need: Render a per-job close-up and changed-pixel count at detail scale alongside the glance render, so the judge can see small detail changes instead of marking them neutral.
evidence: Most neutral verdicts (plinth, wall field, lintels, sills, chute, wall texture) said the change was too faint to see at full-build scale, so the judge could not assess it.

need: Hang a banner as one clean full-height panel on a pilaster or column face with a fixed width, no broken slivers, and an optional lantern hung below it.
evidence: JOB 7 teal banners read as a striped patch with a stray lantern off the column edge; JOB 2 banners became fragmented slivers with floating white bits

need: Lay out a short word or phrase as legible block-letter strokes across a sign band at a given height and width, with a fallback that reads as a plaque when the letters cannot fit.
evidence: JOB 1 gold lettering read as scattered gold blocks and orange teeth, not legible DEEPSLATE HOLDINGS text

need: Default pilasters and quoins to proud depth 2 with a contrasting role material, since depth 1 in the wall material is invisible at glance scale.
evidence: JOB 2 pilasters proud of the wall and dark quoins: before and after renders nearly identical; JOB 8 pier capitals and base blocks not visible

need: Show sub-block relief at a readable scale (close oblique view plus a before/after diff highlight) so the judge can see small finish changes.
evidence: JOB 4, JOB 8, JOB 21, JOB 26, JOB 35: before and after crops look identical, so real relief changes are unverifiable

tool: visibility / exposure check (proposed: mcd check visible)
need: Flag any detail placement that has no exposed face in the standard views, before the build is accepted.
evidence: JOB 16 flagpole rod changed no visible pixels in any view

tool: railing round any flat top (detail-language JOB 4 railing)
need: Run a single-height railing round the perimeter of any flat roof or tower top, with regular posts, a continuous top rail, and no pickets poking above merlons or parapets.
evidence: JOB 15 tower-top railing: stray pickets, uneven cross-bars, cluttered spiky tangle instead of a clean rail

need: Offer a slender gold or accent-role spire finial for gable peaks and roof ends, with the material drawn from the palette role rather than a bright default.
evidence: JOB 12 finial is an orange-red ball on a thin stalk, clashing with the slate and gold palette; concept has slender gold spires

need: Build a continuous stair-stepped raking band that follows the roof pitch with no gaps, at a set thickness and material, along both gable edges.
evidence: JOB 10 raking band came out thinner, ragged at half-height steps, and partly lost in shading

need: Anchor the chimney through the roof slope into the roof, with a dark masonry role material and a cap course, so it does not float as a pale column.
evidence: JOB 17 flat-topped light-grey column clashes with deepslate and its cap is stuck to a stray roof fragment

need: Default the crow-step depth to at least 2 with a contrasting cap so the stair-stepping reads at glance scale.
evidence: JOB 33 stepped dark cap and crenellations are barely visible and do not add the concept's gable stair-stepping

tool: arch (shapes-curved) for window and door heads
need: Use the arch or segmental hood for window and door openings so the arched profile reads at the detail scale, not just a lintel strip.
evidence: JOB 21 arched ground-floor windows show only a darker lintel strip; JOB 32 side door 'stone arch' shows no arch profile; JOB 35 side window lintels barely change

tool: thin element brush (posts, rails, downpipes; proposed B.post)
need: Place posts, handrails, downpipes and gate posts at a minimum section (2 wide or a capped 1-wide) in a palette role colour, so they read as members rather than sticks or stubs.
evidence: JOB 18 handrails are two small sticks; JOB 24 gate posts are thin stubs; JOB 30 post-and-rail strip is barely visible; JOB 31 downpipe became tan posts in the wrong colour

need: Place planters and shrubs as small volumes (about 3x2 footprint, 2 high) with a leaf or flower palette, so they read as planting at glance scale.
evidence: JOB 22 planters are a few tiny dark-green and purple specks, too small to read as shrubs or flower beds

need: Offer a louvre vent with alternating slats and dark gaps, so the vent reads as a vent rather than a faint plank streak.
evidence: JOB 14 tower-head vent change is a faint lighter-plank streak with no profile or depth

tool: window grid / mullion preset for glass faces
need: Offer a mullion grid preset for glass panes (spacing, frame material, depth) so the glass shaft reads as crisp mullions instead of flat dark glass.
evidence: JOB 26 mullion grid is only faintly different from the before state, with flat glass and no crafted depth

tool: palette by role (role to block mapping)
need: Map 'white' or 'quartz' roles to a quartz or white block, and 'accent gold' to a gold block, so trim and bands match the concept colour rather than falling back to light grey.
evidence: JOB 27 quartz cap and bands read as a mismatched thin grey strip instead of white quartz

need: Give lintels, hoods and sills a projection depth and profile option (e.g. depth 1-2 with a stair or slab step), so any rectangular opening gets a surround that casts shade instead of a flat recolour on the wall face.
evidence: JOB 6 (west hood stub and sill barely read), JOB 7 (lintels are thin dark slabs with no hood profile or depth), JOB 9 (jambs add no visible depth)

need: Add a mullion/glazing-bar option to any window opening (cross or vertical bars in a chosen frame block) so panes read as divided windows, not blank panels.
evidence: JOB 10 glazing change gave flat pale panes with almost no mullion detail

tool: cornice / parapet coping / string course (detailing cornice <F>, cornice, coping)
need: Give cornices, coping and storey string courses a projection depth of at least 2 with a dentil or corbel rhythm option, and a preset that places a string course at every storey line; the current default projects too little to read at elevation scale.
evidence: JOB 7 (eave ledge nearly invisible), JOB 8 (belt courses faint), JOB 10 (roof coping barely visible), JOB 12 (heavy dentilled cornice and string course not produced)

tool: render views for small features (elevation scale)
need: Render a close-up crop around each detail job's target cells, so 1-2 block features (finials, lanterns, flagpoles, shrubs in front of them) are visible to the judge and the builder.
evidence: JOB 14 (finial a faint spike), JOB 17 (flagpole a single block, barely visible), JOB 24 (lantern a dot, half-buried in foliage)

need: Deterministic vertical-element brush: a pole with an optional cap or ball, placed on any apex or roof point, with height and width scaled to the feature so it reads as a finial, flagpole or post at normal viewing distance.
evidence: JOB 14 (pediment finial too small), JOB 17 (tower flagpole one block), JOB 24 (lantern posts at plinth ends unreadable)

need: Place a potted tree or shrub prop (pot block plus leaf or sapling mass, at least 2 blocks tall) into a named bay or corner, so it reads as a plant and not as a green sliver.
evidence: JOB 25 (two thin green strips read as slivers, not potted trees)

need: When a paint or detail rule writes zero cells, fail loudly with the reason (e.g. skipped as already detailed) and offer force as the default for cells a job explicitly targets; never report success on a zero-cell write.
evidence: JOB 13 (pediment rake changed no pixels), JOB 20 (entrance doors no pixels), JOB 36 (edge piers no pixels). Session notes: paint skipped already-detailed cells (0 written); weather rule wrote 0 cells on stone_bricks roof face

need: Apply an arch or segmental head to an existing rectangular ground-floor window or door opening in place, without rebuilding the wall around it.
evidence: JOB 28 (ground windows show no arched heads), JOB 38 (side door arch shows only a faint grey patch)

need: Deterministic classical capital and base brush for pilasters and columns (a 1-2 block capital and plinth step) that fits any column or pilaster width, so the column heads and bases read as ornamented, not as plain shafts.
evidence: JOB 9 (pilaster capitals and bases not readable), JOB 12 (portico capitals only a faint lighter band)

need: Add a contrast-strength and mottling-density parameter to the vary and weather rules, with a visible preset, so stone and deepslate variation reads at elevation scale.
evidence: JOB 1 (north facade texture barely perceptible), JOB 2 (west cracked-deepslate mottling barely registers)

need: Report a per-job pixel-delta measure and a close-up before/after crop, so the judge can tell 'changed but too small' from 'changed nothing' and stops reading small deltas as neutral.
evidence: Most neutral detail jobs (JOB 9, 10, 25, 28) look identical before and after at elevation scale; the judge cannot separate these from no-ops

need: Place a raised-panel tablet with inset, legible lettering on a wall band, keeping its frame, panel relief and clearance from adjacent posts or signs.
evidence: JOB 3 INSPECTORATE plaque: raised carved panels became flat pale stone plus dark blocks and a wood post cutting the sign band; reads patchy, not a plaque.

need: Default to a grounded, stepped finial seated on a roof or pediment cell with no air gap; a 1-block rod off a roof edge must not be an option.
evidence: JOB 7: thin stone rods float at roof corners and pediment feet, reading as antennae with some hovering off the eave.

need: Flag detail blocks with no supporting neighbour or no owning role (floating rods, protruding stubs, stray patches) before render.
evidence: JOB 7 floating finials; JOB 35 stray protruding cornice stubs; JOB 12 stray tan blocks on white piers; JOB 24 stray pale block.

tool: mcd render (banner / entity blocks in glance views)
need: Make placed banners visible in the standard front and front-left close-ups, or report that they are not rendered.
evidence: JOB 11: teal corner banners do not appear in front or front-left close-ups; only a tan block change shows.

tool: downpipe (vertical run, gutter to ground; proposed: B.downpipe)
need: Run a continuous vertical pipe in a chosen material down a pier or corner from roof edge to ground, with a material and tone that match the palette role.
evidence: JOB 12: two tan/terracotta blocks at window height, no vertical run; JOB 33: faint mossy strips barely change the read.

need: Mount a lantern on a bracket projecting from a pier face at a set offset, sized to read at street scale, rather than on a thin chain stub.
evidence: JOB 13: tiny lanterns on a thin dark chain stub, slightly off the pier in the front elevation.

need: Offer a stepped corbelled arch profile over openings with a contrasting voussoir material so the arch reads in the silhouette.
evidence: JOB 15: corbelled arches over shopfront bays show only as faint stair-step notches in the pale stone.

need: Draw mullions in the frame material rather than a tint, so the grid reads on glass at street scale.
evidence: JOB 16: mullion grid shows only faint light-blue lines on the glass.

need: Add transom and sidelight variants for double and single doors, with framing that reads at a glance.
evidence: JOB 17: transom change is tiny and barely shifts the read against the concept's double door.

need: Place potted shrubs or clipped topiary on a plinth or in a planter, with a footprint and height that show from the street.
evidence: JOB 19: potted shrubs and topiary changed no visible pixels in any view.

need: Report each detail job's changed-cell count and visible-pixel delta, and flag jobs that changed nothing as failed rather than as successful edits.
evidence: JOB 18 (entrance steps), JOB 19 (shrubs), JOB 22 (furnishings), JOB 34 (dentil): no pixels changed, with no warning.

need: Include an interior or eye-level view in the default glance set when a job touches interiors, and show single-block changes at a readable scale.
evidence: JOB 22 interior furnishings invisible in exterior views; JOB 24 one-block paving change and JOB 25 moss flecks too small to judge.

tool: relief projection presets (sill <F>, pier, trim, cornice <F>, coping, planter ledges)
need: Default relief projection to at least 2 blocks so sills, pilasters, ledges, coping and eave brackets read at street scale; 1-block defaults vanish.
evidence: JOB 20 planter ledges, JOB 27 pilasters, JOB 36 eave brackets, JOB 39 coping, JOB 35 cornice: thin, barely visible relief.

need: Place shutters flanking the opening outside the glazing, so the glass and mullions stay in place.
evidence: JOB 31: shutters replaced the glazed window with a black void and thin slats, so the windows read as holes.

need: Offer a continuous projecting cornice course with a dentil or bracket rhythm that returns cleanly at corners, with no detached side stubs.
evidence: JOB 35 cornice shows stray stubs at the sides; JOB 36 eave brackets barely visible; JOB 34 dentil row changed no pixels.

need: Give posts a capital and base profile option so a recolour is never the only change to a post.
evidence: JOB 38: arcade posts were only recoloured to a darker, flatter tone with no new profile.

need: Provide a density preset strong enough to read as weathering at building scale, with a visible default.
evidence: JOB 25: moss and cracking show only faint flecks on the plinth; the change is too subtle to register.

tool: palette role-conflict check (proposed: mcd palette check)
need: Flag blocks whose tone breaks their role's contrast (for example light tan on a white pier, or pale blocks on dark stone) before the render.
evidence: JOB 12 tan blocks on white piers; JOB 24 pale weathered block against dark stone.

need: Widening a pier or post to two blocks must keep the wall plane flat and take the wall's own material family, with no stepped or ragged edge, and should refuse a lighter-toned material than the surrounding frame by default.
evidence: JOB 6: widened piers render as pale flat light-oak blocks with a ragged stepped edge on the right pier, clashing with the darker concept tone.

tool: glance render and per-job visibility report
need: Each detail job should report how many judged-view pixels or cells actually changed, and jobs below a visibility floor should be flagged as invisible at glance scale instead of shown as neutral changes.
evidence: JOB 8, 11, 15, 16, 19, 25, 26, 37: before/after renders are nearly identical or the change is too small to read, so the judge cannot tell whether the job helped or hurt.

need: A shutter treatment that builds a panel-shaped closed shutter sized to the window opening (louvred or panelled, with a visible gap at the frame edge), rather than thin full-height slats.
evidence: JOB 14: the 'shutters' render as two thin vertical brown slats running full window height, so the opening reads as dark and empty.

need: Lanterns hung from a pier, bracket or overhang should attach through a chain or bracket to a solid support, align to the building's existing lantern row, and use the build's lantern type; the helper should refuse a placement with no support or an offset from the row.
evidence: JOB 15: one hanging lantern reads as a stray floating block at the edge. JOB 23: a second bracket and lantern sit on a different level and are offset from the existing lantern, forming a cluttered duplicate pair.

need: Before a detail job is accepted, check that new accent blocks (lanterns, caps, rods, gold or copper trim) belong to the build's palette family and flag any hue that clashes with the existing accent.
evidence: JOB 16: gold caps read as odd yellow blocks. JOB 23: cyan soul lantern clashes with the warm lantern palette. JOB 34: bright orange copper cap does not match the dark slate roof.

need: The arch helper should offer a stepped or corbelled head over a rectangular bay, with an optional keystone block, so shopfront and door heads can match a stepped-arch concept.
evidence: JOB 19: arch heads over shopfront bays are a small grey block, not the stepped-arch profile. JOB 26: the gold keystone is not visible because no keystone option exists.

tool: post / colonnade helper with base and capital
need: A post or colonnade treatment should build a column with a base and capital, keep clear of attached lanterns and banners, and avoid a flat slab-like silhouette.
evidence: JOB 31: flat near-black posts stick out of the side return as a bare slab, with unfinished gaps at the base, and they partly hide the lantern and banner.

tool: stair and step helper with support check (nosed treads, cheeks)
need: A step helper should fill the support course under every tread and cheek, then run a void check that reports see-through holes or unsupported cells in the facade.
evidence: JOB 27: the change opens a see-through hole in the bottom step course and a gap beside the cheek, creating broken voids and a ragged silhouette.

need: A chimney should seat on the local roof plane by extending down to the sloped surface under its footprint, and it should offer a replace-existing mode so the old chimney is removed rather than left beside the new one.
evidence: JOB 34: the new chimney is a wide detached block floating off the roof slope with a visible gap beneath, and the old thin chimney is still standing beside it.
